name: P2 · Previous-year papers — Computer Science (KEA / KSET)
description: Real questions from past KEA / KSET papers (90 so far): KSET 2024 – Computer Science & Application. Typed from KEA's scanned question papers with the options in the printed order; each question shows its paper and number. Where KEA publishes no full key, the answer was worked out by ExamSim and says so. Each paper also comes as a full-paper mock test.

questions.question: Which one of the following logical equivalences involve biconditional statements?
questions.subject: Q1–25
questions.explanation: Only option 4 uses the biconditional ↔; the others use implication, disjunction and conjunction. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question:
From the following arguments, determine whether they are correct or incorrect.
(i) Ice cream is delicious to eat. Rahul's dessert is not ice cream. Therefore, Rahul's dessert is not delicious to eat.
(ii) All registered voters are eligible to participate in elections. Ranjith is not eligible to participate in elections. Therefore, Ranjith is not a registered voter.
questions.subject: Q1–25
questions.explanation: (i) commits the fallacy of denying the antecedent; (ii) is valid by modus tollens (P → Q, ¬Q ⊢ ¬P). (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Relation R is defined on set A = {a, b, c, d, e}, where R = {(a,d), (b,c), (c,a), (d,e)}. Determine if R forms a tree. If it does, find the root.

options.B: R is a tree with root a
options.C: R is a tree with root b
options.D: R is a tree with root d

questions.subject: Q1–25
questions.explanation: The edges form the path b → c → a → d → e: connected, acyclic, and b is the only vertex with in-degree 0, so b is the root. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Which one of the following expressions is in canonical SoP form considering A, B, C as Boolean variables?
questions.subject: Q1–25
questions.explanation: In canonical sum-of-products form every product term (minterm) contains all the variables, complemented or not. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: The chances of a defective material in three boxes x, y and z are 1/5, 1/6 and 1/7 respectively. A box is selected at random and the material drawn is found to be defective. Find the probability that it came from box A.
questions.subject: Q1–25
questions.explanation: The paper says 'box A' for the first box, x. Bayes: (1/3·1/5) / (1/3·(1/5 + 1/6 + 1/7)) = (42/210) / (107/210) = 42/107. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question:
Match the following terms related to the given Pigeonhole principle scenario and choose the correct answer.
a) Pigeonhole principle
b) Contradiction
c) Assigned Pigeons
d) Overcrowded hole
i. States that when m < n, not all pigeons can be assigned
ii. More than one pigeon assigned to the same pigeonhole
iii. Each pigeonhole contains at most one pigeon
iv. The assumption that all pigeons are assigned

options.A: a – i, b – iv, c – iii, d – ii
options.B: a – ii, b – i, c – iii, d – iv
options.C: a – i, b – ii, c – iv, d – iii
options.D: a – iii, b – ii, c – i, d – iv

questions.subject: Q1–25
questions.explanation: The proof assumes every pigeon gets its own hole (iv) and derives a contradiction; an overcrowded hole holds more than one pigeon. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Let G be a group of order 6; H be a subgroup of G, such that 1 < |H| < 6. Choose the best option from below.

options.A: Both G and H may not be cyclic
options.B: G may not be cyclic; but H is always cyclic
options.C: G is always cyclic; but H may not be cyclic
options.D: Both G and H are always cyclic

questions.subject: Q1–25
questions.explanation: G may be S₃, which is not cyclic. By Lagrange, |H| is 2 or 3 – a prime – and every group of prime order is cyclic. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question:
Match the following terms with their correct definitions and choose the correct option.
a) Weighted Graph
b) Weight
c) Unweighted Graph
i. A graph with no labelled edges
ii. A graph where each edge has a numerical value
iii. A numerical value associated with an edge
iv. A graph that has no vertices

options.A: a – ii, b – iii, c – i
options.B: a – i, b – iv, c – ii
options.C: a – ii, b – i, c – iii
options.D: a – iii, b – ii, c – iv

questions.subject: Q1–25
questions.explanation: A weighted graph has a number on each edge; that number is the weight; an unweighted graph has no such labels. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question:
Given the following Linear Programming Problem,
minimize Z = 6x + 3y
subject to the constraints
4x + y ≥ 80
x + 5y ≥ 115
3x + 2y ≤ 150
x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0
The minimum value of Z is ____
questions.subject: Q1–25
questions.explanation: Corner points: (15, 20) → 150; (2, 72) → 228; (40, 15) → 285. The minimum is 150 at x = 15, y = 20. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Which algorithm includes repeated addition of two predetermined values A and B to a product P and then performs a rightward arithmetic shift on P?
questions.subject: Q1–25
questions.explanation: Booth's multiplication algorithm adds or subtracts the multiplicand and then arithmetic-shifts the product register right. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question:
For the given decimal number 1234,
(i) Hexadecimal equivalent is 4D2
(ii) Octal equivalent is 2322
From the above statements choose the correct option
questions.subject: Q1–25
questions.explanation: 4·256 + 13·16 + 2 = 1234 and 2·512 + 3·64 + 2·8 + 2 = 1234. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: The time between the receival of an interrupt and its service is called
questions.subject: Q1–25
questions.explanation: Interrupt latency is the delay from the interrupt request to the start of its service routine. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Which one of the following statements is TRUE for memory-mapped I/O?

options.A: The I/O devices have separate address space
options.B: The I/O devices and memory share the same address space
options.C: A part of the memory is specially set aside for I/O operation
options.D: The memory and I/O devices have an associated address space

questions.subject: Q1–25
questions.explanation: In memory-mapped I/O, device registers occupy addresses in the same address space as memory and are accessed with ordinary load/store instructions. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question:
In a pipeline unit, with K stages and n instructions,
(i) Speedup of the pipeline unit compared to sequential processor is Kn / (K + (n − 1))
(ii) The pipeline has to be flushed if the pipeline unit encounters branch instruction.
From the above statements choose the correct option
questions.subject: Q1–25
questions.explanation: Sequential time nK cycles vs pipelined K + n − 1 cycles; a taken branch invalidates the instructions already fetched behind it. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: In Relative Addressing Mode, the effective address = ____

options.B: address part of instruction + index register
options.C: address part of instruction + base register
options.D: address part of instruction + register indirect

questions.subject: Q1–25
questions.explanation: Relative (PC-relative) mode adds the address field to the program counter; index and base modes use other registers. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question:
Which one of the following is a form of "locality of reference"?
(i) temporal
(ii) spatial
(iii) write-through
(iv) sequential
questions.subject: Q1–25
questions.explanation: Write-through is a cache write policy, not a kind of locality. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: How many switch points are there in a crossbar switch network that connects 9 processors to 6 memory modules?
questions.subject: Q1–25
questions.explanation: A crossbar has one crosspoint for every processor–memory pair: 9 × 6 = 54. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question:
How many times will the following C loop execute?
for (j = 1; j <= 10; j = j - 1)
questions.subject: Q1–25
questions.explanation: j starts at 1 and keeps decreasing, so j <= 10 stays true: the loop never terminates normally. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Which function is used to remove characters from a string in C++?
questions.subject: Q26–50
questions.explanation: std::string::erase removes characters; std::remove only reorders a range and needs erase to shrink the string. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: In the Digital Differential Analyser algorithm, the decision to increment either x or y is based on:

options.B: The product of x and y coordinates
options.D: Whether the slope is greater than 1 or less than 1

questions.subject: Q26–50
questions.explanation: DDA steps by 1 along the axis of greater change: x when |m| ≤ 1, y when |m| > 1. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: We rotate a point P(2,5) by 60° about a pivot point (1,2). The new transformed point P' would be ____
questions.subject: Q26–50
questions.explanation: Relative to the pivot the point is (1, 3). Rotating: x = 0.5 − 3(0.866) ≈ −2.10, y = 0.866 + 1.5 ≈ 2.37. Adding the pivot gives ≈ (−1.1, 4.4), i.e. (−1, 4). (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: The algorithm that is typically used to compute points on a Bezier curve is ____
questions.subject: Q26–50
questions.explanation: de Casteljau's algorithm evaluates a Bézier curve by repeated linear interpolation of its control points. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: In the Cohen-Sutherland line clipping algorithm, the region codes (out codes) are:
questions.subject: Q26–50
questions.explanation: One bit each for above, below, right and left of the clip window: 9 regions, 4-bit codes. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question:
Which of the following can act as possible termination conditions in K-means?
(a) For a fixed number of iterations
(b) The assignment of observations to clusters does not change between iterations except for cases with a bad local minimum
(c) Centroids do not change between successive iterations
(d) Terminate when reduction in the sum of square distances between points and their assigned cluster centroids falls below threshold.
questions.subject: Q26–50
questions.explanation: All four are standard stopping criteria for K-means. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: What is the process of examining large and varied data sets to uncover hidden patterns, unknown correlations, market trends, customer preferences and other useful information?
questions.subject: Q26–50
questions.explanation: Discovering hidden patterns and correlations in data is data mining (the analytics step of KDD). (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question:
Match the following and choose the correct option:
a) Document-oriented database
b) Key-value database
c) Column-oriented database
d) Graph databases
i. HBase
ii. Neo4J
iii. Redis
iv. MongoDB

options.A: a – ii, b – iv, c – iii, d – i
options.B: a – ii, b – iii, c – iv, d – i
options.C: a – iv, b – iii, c – i, d – ii
options.D: a – ii, b – i, c – iii, d – iv

questions.subject: Q26–50

questions.question: The Relational Algebra does not have
questions.subject: Q26–50
questions.explanation: Basic relational algebra has selection, projection, set operations, products, joins and division; aggregation is an extension. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Which one of the following statements is FALSE?

options.A: Candidate keys are the minimal keys whose superset is not a subkey
options.B: Dependent entities are also called as weak entities
options.C: Generalization is a relationship that exists between a higher-level entity set and the lower-level entity set
options.D: A relationship is an association among entities

questions.subject: Q26–50
questions.explanation: A candidate key is a minimal superkey – no proper subset of it is a superkey. Statement 1 does not state this. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question:
Let R1(a,b,c) and R2(x,y,z) be two relations in which 'a' is foreign key of R1 that refers to the primary key of R2. Consider the following four options:
(a) Insert into R1
(b) Insert into R2
(c) Delete from R1
(d) Delete from R2
Which of the following is correct about the referential integrity constraint with respect to above?
questions.subject: Q26–50
questions.explanation: Inserting into the referencing relation R1 may add a dangling foreign key; deleting from the referenced relation R2 may orphan R1 rows. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Which one of the following statements is FALSE?

options.A: In Discretionary Access Control, the owner can determine the access privileges
options.B: Discretionary Access Control has tighter security compared to Mandatory Access Control
options.C: Discretionary Access Control is flexible with no rules and regulations
options.D: Decisions will be based on the identity of the user and ownership in Discretionary Access Control

questions.subject: Q26–50
questions.explanation: Mandatory Access Control, with system-enforced labels, is the stricter model; DAC is flexible and owner-controlled. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: In a distributed system environment the location transparency allows the database users, programmers and administrators to treat the data as if it resides in a single location. An SQL query with location transparency needs to specify ____
questions.subject: Q26–50
questions.explanation: With location (but not fragmentation) transparency, a query names the fragments but not the sites where they are stored. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Data selection deals with the

options.A: actual discovery phase of a knowledge discovery process
options.B: data collection and selection of right data for KDD process
options.C: a subject-oriented, time-variant data collection in support of environment

questions.subject: Q26–50
questions.explanation: Selection is the first KDD step: choosing the relevant data. Options 3 and 4 describe a data warehouse. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: A section of code or set of operations in which a process may be changing shared variables is known as a ____
questions.subject: Q26–50
questions.explanation: Code that accesses shared data must run under mutual exclusion – the critical section. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question:
Given below are two statements: One is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R)
Assertion (A): Random Access Memory (RAM) is volatile and stores data/programs currently in use.
Reason (R): RAM is a storage medium that retains its contents even after the supply of electricity has been turned off.

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

questions.subject: Q26–50
questions.explanation: RAM is volatile – it loses its contents when power is removed – so R is false. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: ____ is the disk scheduling algorithm used in Solid State Drives (SSDs)
questions.subject: Q26–50
questions.explanation: SSDs have no seek time, so a simple FCFS (NOOP) policy is typically used. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question:
Listed below are some Operating System abstractions and the hardware components. Which matching pair is correct?
a) Thread
b) Virtual address space
c) File system
d) Signal
i. Interrupt
ii. Memory
iii. CPU
iv. Disc

options.A: a – iii, b – ii, c – iv, d – i
options.B: a – iii, b – iv, c – i, d – ii
options.C: a – ii, b – iii, c – iv, d – i
options.D: a – iv, b – ii, c – i, d – iii

questions.subject: Q26–50
questions.explanation: Threads abstract the CPU, address spaces abstract memory, file systems abstract the disk and signals abstract interrupts. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: ____ is a popular cryptographic algorithm for digital signatures and public key infrastructure.
questions.subject: Q26–50
questions.explanation: RSA is a public-key algorithm used for signatures and PKI; MD5 and SHA-1 are hashes and AES is symmetric. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: In ____ technique, Virtual Memory Managers (VMMs) do not virtualize real hardware but instead create an optimized virtual system.
questions.subject: Q26–50
questions.explanation: In programming-environment virtualization (e.g. the Java VM), the VMM presents an optimised virtual system rather than real hardware. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question:

b) A file object
c) A super block object
d) A dentry object
i. Represents an entire file system

iv. Represents an individual file

questions.question: What are the phases of the Adaptive Software Development Model?

options.B: Requirements, Analysis, Design, Evolution and Delivery
options.C: Feasibility Study, Business Study, Functional Model Iteration, Design and Build Iteration, Implementation

questions.subject: Q51–75
questions.explanation: ASD (Highsmith) cycles through speculation, collaboration and learning; option 3 lists the DSDM phases. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of Sprint Retrospective in SCRUM FRAMEWORK?

options.A: To plan for another Scrum's Sprint
options.B: To review test cases from the beginning
options.C: To review the past Scrum's Sprint and identify any improvement

questions.subject: Q51–75
questions.explanation: The retrospective inspects how the last sprint went and plans improvements; sprint planning is a separate event. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: The first step in writing a use case is to define the set of ____ that will be involved in the story.
questions.subject: Q51–75
questions.explanation: Pressman: the first step in writing a use case is to define the actors. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: How to estimate the effort using cost per person-month to calculate total cost of a software, if it has 10 persons-months and the average cost per person-month as $5000. The total cost is:
questions.subject: Q51–75
questions.explanation: 10 person-months × $5,000 = $50,000. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question:
Consider the given statements.
Statement 1: Cost of conducting technical reviews for Software Engineering work products
Statement 2: Cost of data collection and metrics evaluation
Statement 3: Cost of testing and debugging
These statements are the examples of ____
questions.subject: Q51–75
questions.explanation: Pressman lists technical reviews, data collection and metrics evaluation, and testing and debugging as appraisal costs. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: ____ approach is used when a project encompasses the use of existing software that must be modified in some way as part of a project
questions.subject: Q51–75
questions.explanation: Change sizing estimates the modifications (reuse, adding, changing, deleting code) made to existing software. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: A timeline chart is also called ____
questions.subject: Q51–75
questions.explanation: Pressman: a timeline chart is also called a Gantt chart. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: A software is requiring 5000 Lines (LoC). Using basic COCOMO model, the effort E is calculated as E = 3 × (KLoC)^1.2. With these details, derive the estimated effort rightly in person-months.
questions.subject: Q51–75
questions.explanation: 5000 LoC = 5 KLoC, so E = 3 × 5^1.2 ≈ 20.7 person-months. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: A ____ complements the technical review by assessing a configuration object for characteristics that are generally not considered during the review.
questions.subject: Q51–75
questions.explanation: Pressman: the software configuration audit complements the technical review. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question:
A software processes user requests and produces responses as below:
• Number of Inputs: 4
• Number of Outputs: 2
What is the 'functional independence' based on the 'output to input' ratio?
questions.subject: Q51–75
questions.explanation: As the question defines it, the ratio is outputs / inputs = 2 / 4 = 0.5. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: The average time complexity of quick sort is ____
questions.subject: Q51–75
questions.explanation: Quick sort averages O(N log N); its worst case is O(N²). (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: In a complete binary tree, if an element is assigned the number i (where 1 ≤ i ≤ n), then which of the following statements is TRUE regarding its children?

options.A: If 2i + 1 > n, the element has no right child
options.B: If 2i > n, the element has a left child
options.C: The left child is always assigned the number 2i − 1
options.D: The right child is assigned the number 2i

questions.subject: Q51–75
questions.explanation: With 1-based numbering the children of i are 2i and 2i + 1; a child exists only if its number is ≤ n. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: What is the primary advantage of using balanced search trees, such as AVL or red-black trees, for solving a histogramming problem when the number of distinct keys m is small compared to n?

options.A: They require more memory to store all keys
options.B: They are easier to implement than sorting methods
options.C: They can solve the problem in O(m × n) time
options.D: They can solve the problem in O(n log m) time

questions.subject: Q51–75
questions.explanation: Each of the n keys is looked up or inserted in a tree of at most m nodes: O(n log m), better than sorting in O(n log n). (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Which one of the following is not a step of Dynamic Programming?

options.A: Characterize the structure of optimal solutions
options.B: Recursively defines the values of optimal solutions
options.C: Compute the value of optimal solutions in a Bottom-Up minimum
options.D: Compute the value of optimal solutions in a Top-Down minimum

questions.subject: Q51–75

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is TRUE when AVL search trees are utilized to represent a dictionary, ensuring that each dictionary operation is performed in logarithmic time?
(i) The height of an AVL tree with n elements/nodes is O(log n) and for every value of n, n ≥ 0, there exists an AVL tree
(ii) An n element AVL search tree can be searched in O(height) = O(log n) time
(iii) A new element can be inserted into an n-element AVL search tree so that the result is an n + 1 element AVL tree and such insertion can be done in O(log n) time

questions.subject: Q51–75
questions.explanation: All four properties hold for AVL trees (Sahni). (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: ____ are a set of problems that can be solved in polynomial time by deterministic algorithms.

questions.explanation: P is the class of problems decidable in deterministic polynomial time. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: ____ is performed to reduce the likelihood of the erroneous outputs in randomized algorithms.

questions.explanation: Probability amplification repeats a randomised algorithm independently to drive the error probability down. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: The Halting Problem for a Turing Machine is

options.B: Solvable for deterministic Turing Machines only
options.C: Solvable if the machine has a finite tape

questions.subject: Q51–75
questions.explanation: Turing (1936): no algorithm decides, for every TM and input, whether the machine halts. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Which one of the following instances of the Post Correspondence Problem has a viable sequence?
questions.subject: Q51–75
questions.explanation: Pairs 1, 2, 3, 3 give ab·ba·aa·aa = abbaaaaa on top and abb·aaa·a·a = abbaaaaa below. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Flow of information among the attributes in a parse tree is denoted by
questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: A dependency graph shows the order in which attribute instances must be evaluated. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: The optional access link in the activation record is used for

options.A: pointing to the activation record of the cache
options.B: referring non-local data held in other activation records

questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: The access (static) link points to the activation record of the enclosing scope, for access to non-local names. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: The primary data structure used by an LR parser to keep track of the parsing process is ____
questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: An LR parser shifts states and symbols onto a stack and pops them on reductions. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: If a carrier modulated by a digital bit stream has one of the possible phases of 0, 90, 180 and 270 degrees, such modulation is called as
questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: Four phases, each carrying 2 bits, is quadrature phase-shift keying. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question:
Match the following for IPv4 addressing and select the correct key
a) class A
b) class B
c) class C
d) class D
(i) 2 bytes for network portion, 2 bytes for host portion
(ii) multicasting
(iii) 1 byte for network portion, 3 bytes for host portion
(iv) 3 portions for network portion, 1 byte for host portion

options.A: a – iv, b – i, c – iii, d – ii
options.B: a – iii, b – i, c – iv, d – ii
options.C: a – ii, b – iii, c – i, d – iv
options.D: a – iv, b – ii, c – iii, d – i

questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: Class A = 8 network bits, class B = 16, class C = 24; class D addresses are for multicast. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: A bridge operates at the data link layer giving it access to the ____ address of all the stations connected to it.
questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: A bridge works at layer 2 and filters frames using physical (MAC) addresses. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: For a network with n devices, the number of duplex-mode links required for mesh topology is:
questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: Every pair needs one duplex link: C(n, 2) = n(n − 1)/2. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: The process of dividing an analog signal into a string of discrete outputs, each denoting a constant amplitude is called as
questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: Quantisation maps sampled amplitudes onto a finite set of levels. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: When data and acknowledgement are sent in a same frame, it is known as
questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: Piggybacking attaches the acknowledgement to an outgoing data frame. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: The role of Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) is to find the

options.C: IP address that corresponds to a MAC address
options.D: MAC address that corresponds to an IP address

questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: ARP maps a known IP address to a MAC address on the local network (RARP does the reverse). (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question:
Which of these are TRUE for public-private key encryption algorithm?
(i) Private key of the receiver is used by the sender to encrypt the message
(ii) Public key is used by the receiver to decrypt the message
questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: The sender encrypts with the receiver's public key and the receiver decrypts with its own private key. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question:
Which of these statements are CORRECT?
(i) When a router receives the packet, TTL is reduced by one
(ii) When a router receives the packet, TTL is increased by one
(iii) If the TTL count is zero and the packet has not reached the destination, the packet is discarded
(iv) If the TTL count is 255 and the packet has not reached the destination, the packet is discarded
questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: Each router decrements TTL and discards the packet when TTL reaches zero. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: The Mobile Application Part (MAP) is a/an ____ protocol that provides an application layer for the various nodes in GSM and UMTS mobile core networks and GPRS core networks.
questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: MAP is an application-layer protocol of the SS7 (Signalling System No. 7) stack. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: What is the Turing Test designed to assess?
questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: Turing's imitation game tests whether a machine's conversational behaviour is indistinguishable from a human's. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Suppose you are constructing AI for an intergalactic travel planner. What representation handles multiple planets?

options.A: Stacking planets in a priority queue based on their beauty
options.B: A graph connecting planets with worm hole edges for quick travel
options.C: A hash table mapping planets to their languages
options.D: An array of codes to encode planet coordinates

questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: Route planning needs locations as vertices and connections as edges – a graph. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Which one of the following is used to query RDF in semantic web?
questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: SPARQL is the W3C query language for RDF data. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Which technique considers the problem of extracting a reward function from observed optimal behaviour of an expert acting in an environment?
questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: Inverse RL infers the reward from demonstrations; ordinary RL learns behaviour from a given reward. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Fuzzy equivalence relation is a type of fuzzy relation that satisfies
questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: Like a crisp equivalence relation, a fuzzy equivalence (similarity) relation is reflexive, symmetric and (max–min) transitive. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: In a multilayer perceptron, the back propagation algorithm is used

options.A: As it initializes the weights of networks
options.D: To propagate errors back through network to update the weights

questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: Backpropagation computes error gradients layer by layer, backwards, for weight updates. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Which one of the following is not a specified method that is used for the selection of parents?
questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: Elitism copies the best individuals unchanged into the next generation; it is not a parent-selection scheme. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Which one of the following algorithm is commonly used for classification tasks in AI?
questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: Decision trees are supervised classifiers; K-means is unsupervised clustering. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)
